summary: Reversing the full list changes every internal next edge, so a linear number of pointer updates is unavoidable. The current bounded reversal visits the prefix and segment once and matches that bound.

optimality.argument: Use the legal case left = 1 and right = n. The original list has n - 1 forward edges between consecutive nodes, while the required result has all n - 1 of those edges reversed; producing it therefore requires Omega(n) link changes. The current algorithm advances at most left - 1 times to the segment, reverses exactly right - left + 1 nodes, and performs constant reconnection work, for O(n) total time.

replacement_checks.evidence: A full-list reversal replaces the direction of each of the n - 1 internal next edges, requiring a linear number of pointer mutations.
The prefix-location and bounded-reversal loops together execute at most 2n iterations, followed by constant boundary reconnection work.

The source-fidelity-verified examples cover an internal segment and the one-node no-op boundary; black-box real-test execution verifies all existing ordinary checks without inspecting their definitions.
